findings.evidence: In openspec/specs/publication-recovery/spec.md:204 the sentence "Once an exact pull request is selected or created, required-check reads, merge requests ... SHALL use a stable PR number or URL ..." and "A branch-name-only lookup, command exit code, or stale merged PR SHALL NOT authorize destructive cleanup or terminal success." carry no mode qualifier. The candidate's ADDED "Selected exact PR operations use a stable PR identity and the expected head" and "Branch-name lookups and exit codes do not authorize cleanup or success" both begin "For `harness_mode=platform` and `publish_mode=pr`, ...". Their scenarios also add the GIVEN. The same applies to ADDED "A matching publication PR is identified by exact head identity" and "Machine-local cached state is not the authoritative publication cursor", split from paragraph 2 of spec.md:10, which has no qualifier of its own. The qualifier is a condition on the obligation in the original text only for the paragraph 1 sentences. Other ADDED requirements split from unqualified sentences, such as "Merge requests are guarded by the exact validated PR head", stay unqualified, so the treatment is inconsistent.
findings.summary: Some split-out publication-recovery requirements add a `harness_mode=platform`/`publish_mode=pr` qualifier that the original sentence did not carry. This conflicts with design.md's rule that no condition is added.

findings.evidence: The original at platform-rollout spec.md:546 reads "A conflict is safe when either (a) ..., (b) ..., or (c) ... Missing/missing SHALL count as baseline equivalence. Any currently divergent or otherwise unproven path SHALL remain fail-closed." The candidate's MODIFIED requirement keeps only the first and last sentences. The ADDED requirements "A reclaimed migration path matching the target template...", "A path matching the recorded platform template version..." and "A path byte-identical to the target render..." each say "a conflict SHALL count as safe when ...". Only the middle one carries the `Missing/missing` sentence. The scenario under the third requirement adds "only when the byte identity is re-proven from committed `HEAD` after the reset", which the original expresses inside condition (c) rather than as a standalone 'only when'.
findings.summary: The enumerated "(a) or (b) or (c)" definition of a safe Copier recopy conflict is split into three independent "SHALL count as safe when" requirements. The closed list is no longer stated in one place. The `Missing/missing` rule is also attached only to branch (b).
